1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first pulse rate; receiving a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a vehicle; analyzing the second sequence to determine a vehicle proximity condition and a communication capability of the vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second pulse rate based on the analyzed second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate, and wherein the second pulse rate is selected to match the communication capability of the vehicle.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first pulse rate, and wherein the computing device selects the second pulse rate to accommodate a processing speed limitation of the vehicle.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on a loss of signal reception, and transmits a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a third pulse rate, wherein the third pulse rate is faster than the second pulse rate and corresponds to a default transmission rate.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate and is selected based on the communication capability of the third vehicle.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed, and wherein the message is transmitted only via modulated infrared light pulses.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is transmitted via modulated infrared light pulses as a primary communication channel, and optionally also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network as a secondary channel.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of modulated infrared light pulses are received via an IR video sensor mounted on the transmitting vehicle.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of modulated infrared light pulses are received from two or more vehicles simultaneously or sequentially.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles, wherein the fourth pulse rate is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from any of the vehicles.
